fund keeping in view the forthcoming Commonwealth Games in 2010, with a view to
improve its functioning, for providing adequate protection to the people in NCR. The
Committee is of the view that the increase in the allocation for Delhi Police is insufficient,
considering the security scenario of Delhi and the forthcoming Games. The crowded places
of Delhi are the prime targets for terrorist activities due to their vulnerability. One of the
major targets could be Metro Stations. Security at Metro Stations needs to be tightened. The
Committee is also of the view that overall security measures should be strengthened in the
NCR and additional allocation should be made for this purpose. (Para 12.2)
The Committee however expresses its concern over the instances of corruption cases
in Delhi Police as reported in the media. The Committee feels that the system needs to be
overhauled. The Committee hopes that the series of proactive measure undertaken to check
corruption in Delhi Police would ultimately yield results in improving the image of the Delhi
Police in the general police. (Para 12.4)
The Committee takes a serious view of the incidents of road rage. If this is allowed
to happen, it may lead to a chaotic situation where lawlessness becomes the order of the
day. The Committee recommends that severe punishments may be meted out to those
involved in road rage cases and wherever necessary laws may be amended. (Para 12.7)
BUREAU OF IMMIGRATION (BoI)
The Committee notes the progress made in the modernization of BoIs but feels that
latest equipments are required for upgradation of system like equipments which could be
laser compatible so that it could identify counterfeit currencies, foreign countries passports,
etc. The Committee feels that these days the equipments are becoming more advanced and
the credentials of the individuals could be checked with thumb impression, colour of eye,
blood report, etc. The modernization should be aimed at keeping in view the requirement
for next ten years. The Committee also recommends that all ICPs should be covered under
modernization in a phased manner. (Para 13.3)

35
SHIFTING OF BOUNDARIES TO THE ZERO LEVEL
The Committee is of the view that the shifting of the fencing to the zero line is the
only solution left for the convenience of the people residing in nearby villages to carry out
their agricultural activities. The Committee therefore, recommends that suitable action
should be initiated at the earliest for shifting of the fence to zero line. The Committee also
desires that recruitment of female constables be done at the earliest. (Para 14.2)
ILLEGAL BANGLADESHI MIGRANTS
The Committee feels that a large presence of illegal Bangladeshi immigrants poses
a grave threat to the internal security and it should be viewed seriously. Reports have also
appeared that counterfeit notes are in large circulation along Indo-Bangladesh border. The
Committee strongly recommends that movement along the border may be strictly
monitored. (Para 15.4)
BORDER AREA DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME (BADP)
The Committee in its One Hundred thirteenth Report on Demands for Grants
(2005-06) pertaining to the Ministry of DoNER had recommended that it should specify the
developmental work under the Border Area Development Scheme which should be
undertaken around 60-75 Km of the actual border. But the ground realities in this context
are different as the Committee came to know about the fact that these funds are spent on
civilian gardens and parks depriving the people in the border areas where there is hardly
any communication. The Committee recommends that a proper monitoring mechanism
should be put in place to monitor the utilization of these funds as the people living in the
border areas are suffering due to lack of infrastructure viz. schools and other medical
facilities. (Para 16.2)
The Committee feels that border areas in the North-Eastern part of the country have
been neglected for a long time. Even today some border areas are not easily accessible. The
Committee is constraint to note that in spite of its recommendation made in earlier reports,
the Cabinet Secretariat has not taken any decision on the issue of transferring of BADP
scheme to Ministry of DoNER. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the issue be
resolved immediately in the interest of the nation. (Para 16.8)
INSURGENCY IN NORTH-EASTERN STATES
The Committee feels that for the last four or five decades, this region is facing the
problem of insurgency and people are frustrated with the prevailing situation. The
Government has to take on the responsibility of resolving the problem. The Committee is
of the considered view that inspite of decrease in number of the causalities; reported
instances of extortion activities and collection of levies by the outlawed groups are
increasing. The Committee calls upon the Ministry to keep a close watch on the
developments in this regard and all efforts be made to foil the nefarious design of the
secessionists. (Para 17.2)

REPORT
CHAPTER-I
OVERVIEW
1.0 The North Eastern Region of our country consists of eight States of Assam, Arunachal
Pradesh, Meghalaya, Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura and Sikkim which despite having hilly
and inhospitable terrains, porous borders, highly inadequate road links, extremely poor transport
connectivity, limited air services, inadequate rail links and weak telecommunication infrastructure,
has potential to become India’s economic power house. The panoramic setting of the lofty ranges
of the eastern Himalaya, snow peaked mountains, gurgling rivers from Tibet, exotic flora and
fauna, dense forests criss-crossed with network of trekking routes, diverse ethnic cultures and
heritage, the colorful tribal festivals, evergreen forests of Namdapha in Arunachal Pradesh, lush
green grasslands of Kaziranga, the perfect eco-system of Manas in Assam, make this region an
ideal place for tourists particularly for eco and adventurous tourists. Besides, being rich in natural
resources and an energy plus region in terms of hydropower, this region has immense potential to
develop provided certain infrastructure bottlenecks are removed.
1.1 With an objective to convert the untapped potential of North East Region into an opportunity,
the Department of North East Region was formed in September, 2001 which was upgraded to the
status of Ministry of DoNER on 27th May, 2004 by the Government of India for faster socio-
economic development of the region. This Ministry rather than an administrative unit acts as a
facilitator between the Central Ministers/Departments and the State Governments of the North Eastern
Region including Sikkim in the economic development including removal of infrastructural
bottlenecks, provision of basic minimum services, creating an environment for private investment and
to remove impediments to lasting peace and security in the North Eastern Region.
1.2 The Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region seeks to achieve the following goals:
(i) Accelerating the pace of socio-economic development in the North Eastern Region;
(ii) Synergizing the efforts of Central/State Governments/Other Stakeholders for
balanced development of the Region;
(iii) Integrated and holistic planning for the region, taking into account the heightened
consciousness of the people of the region, their aspiration, needs and sensitivities;
(iv) Evolving a c ommon approach for all the agencies working for the development of
the region; and
(v) Formulating appropriate policies for the rapid development of the region.
2.0 The Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961, mandate the Ministry of
DoNER with the following functions:—
(i) Matters relating to the planning, execution and monitoring of developmental
schemes and projects of North Eastern Region including those in the sectors of
Power, Irrigation, Roads and Communications;
(ii) Hill Area Development Programme and Border Area Development Programme in
North Eastern Region;
◆
◆ Included in the original mandate of the Ministry of DoNER but has not been transferred from Planning Commission
and MHA, respectively.

2
(iii) Non-lapsable Central Pool of Resources for North Eastern Region (NLCPR);
(iv) North Eastern Council (NEC);
(v) North East Development Finance Corporation (NEDFi);
(vi) North Eastern Regional Agricultural Marketing Corporation Limited (NERAMAC);
(vii) North Eastern Handloom and Handicrafts Development Corporation (NEHHDC);
(viii) Road works financed in whole or in part by the Central Government in the North
Eastern Region; and
(ix) Planning of Road and Inland Waterways Transport in the North Eastern Region.
2.1 The Ministry implements the work mandated in the Allocation of Business Rules, 1961,
through the formulation of appropriate policies, and implementation of specific Plan Programmes.
The North Eastern Council, Shillong also implements various Plan Schemes in the region.
2.2 The North Eastern Council (NEC), Shillong, an organization under the Ministry, is the
Regional Planning Body for the region. It was set up under the NEC Act, 1971 for securing the
balanced development of the North East. The Minister in charge of the Ministry of Development
of North Eastern Region is the ex-officio Chairman of NEC. Its Members include the Governors
and the Chief Ministers of the eight Member States and three Members nominated by the President
of India.
3.0 In the Tenth Plan period, the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (DoNER)
had been implementing the following Central Plan Schemes:
(a) Advocacy and Publicity,
(b) Technical Assistance and Capacity Building,
(c) Assistance to Sikkim Mining Corporation (SMC),
(d) Assistance to North Eastern Development Finance Corporation Ltd. (NEDFi).
3.1 Besides the above, the following Schemes are also under implementation in the form of
Assistance to the State Plans:
(i) Non-lapsable Central Pool of Resources for North Eastern Region (NLCPR)
(ii) Plan Schemes of the North Eastern Council (NEC)
(iii) Infrastructure development projects under the special package for Bodoland
Territorial Council
(iv) Development of Cities and Roads in the North Eastern States (Externally Aided
Projects)
3.2 Since 1998-99, all non-exempted Ministries/Departments of Government of India are
required to earmark at least 10% of their Gross Budgetary Support (GBS) for the development of
North Eastern States for creation of both economic and social infrastructure such as Power, Roads
and Bridges, Education, Health, Water Supply and Sanitation, etc. in the region. The unutilized
portion of the 10% Plan allocation made by Ministries/Departments is credited at the end of each
financial year in a reserve fund in the Public Account titled ‘Central Resource Pool for Development
of North Eastern Region’ and in administrative parlance known as the Non-Lapsable Central Pool
of Resources (NLCPR). The funds from this Pool are budgeted for financing new infrastructure
projects/schemes in the region under the NLCPR Plan Scheme.

3
3.3 The NLCPR is meant for infrastructure development in almost all the major socio-economic
development sectors. For this purpose, projects are sanctioned for State sector as well as Central
sector. However, the funds available under the Central Pool are not meant to supplement the normal
Plan programmes either of the State Governments or Union Ministries/Departments/Agencies.
4.0 The Ministry also supervises the work of its three enterprises, viz, North Eastern
Handicrafts and Handlooms Development Corporation Ltd. (NEHHDC), North Eastern Regional
Agricultural Marketing Corporation Ltd. (NERAMAC) and North East Development Finance
Corporation (NEDFi).
5.0 While the respective Ministries/Departments are responsible in respect of subjects allocated
to them, the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region coordinates with various Ministries/
Departments of Government of India and the State Governments for various development and
welfare programmes/schemes/activities in North Eastern Region.
6.0 Following the decision of the NEC, eight Special Sectoral Summits have been organized in
different sectors. These sector specific summits have helped in sensitizing both the Central
Government and the States to improve delivery systems and focus attention on the Region and its
issues. The Ministry is actively pursuing the progress of implementation of the recommendations
of these Summits.

7.4 On being asked as to why the development is not visible in North-East Region in spite of
funds being given through different sources, the Secretary, NEC stated as under:
“The whole question of the visibility of what is not taking place in the North-East, I think,
the dimensions are basically two. When we talk of development visibility, I think, there has
been some change. But the requirement of funds that we have done through and we are doing
the Vision-2020 analysis; it came to a staggering amount of Rs. 25,000 crore even to catch
up with the present national per capita income. So, if we have to catch up with this, we
require an investment of Rs. 25,000 crore. But, why is the North-East not getting the visible
sign is that whereas other States are able to attract substantial funds from the private sector,
in the North-East, the only source of funding is the Government source of funding.”
7.5 The Committee is concerned that even though the Ministry of DoNER made a
projection of Rs. 2922 crore for the current year, the actual allocation made was Rs. 1455
crore under plan scheme. The Committee has been given to understand that due to the
reduction in the allocation by almost 50%, many projects would suffer. The Ministry will not
be able to implement the schemes for the development of the region. The Committee,
therefore, strongly recommends that the allocation to the Ministry be made as per its
requirement as it would be in the interest of the overall development of the North-East
Region.
7.6 The Committee is not convinced by the reasoning given by the Secretary, NEC on the
visibility aspect of the development. The component of private investment is a totally
different matter to be viewed in the proper context and perspective. First of all, the
outcome of the public investments should be visible and transparent. Then only a positive
message will go for private investment. The Committee appreciates that there are basic and
inherent problems in converting public investment into tangible results. That can only be
achieved if there is a sense of commitment among implementing agencies and the State
Governments. The Committee recommends that sincere efforts should be made to ensure
that whatever investment is made for the development of NER should yield concrete result
so much so that the outcome should manifest itself.

8.1 NLCPR which was created in 1998, is meant for accrual of the unspent balances of the
10 per cent allocation earmarked in their budget by various Ministries/Departments for North-
eastern region. The Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (DoNER) is provided
budgetary allocation for sanction of infrastructure development projects in the North Eastern States
out of the NLCPR. The broad objective of the NLCPR scheme is to ensure speedy development
of infrastructure in the North Eastern Region by increasing the flow of budgetary financing for
specific infrastructure projects/schemes in the region.
8.2 There are 17 Ministries/Departments, particularly Petroleum and Natural Gas, Social Justice
and Empowerment which have been exempted from allocating the stipulated ten per cent of Gross
Budgetary Support (GBS) for the NE States. According to the Ministry of DoNER the following
criteria are followed for exempting a Ministry/Department from earmarking 10% of their GBS for
the North East:—
(a) Highly scientific Ministries /Departments with hardly any scope for work in the North
East;
(b) The Ministries /Departments having no direct involvement in the North East including
Sikkim such as the erstwhile Department of Ocean Development; and
(c) The Ministries in which case the expenditure in the North Eastern Region was ‘Nil’
during the last three years.
8.3 The Committee was also informed that Government of India does not provide any budgetary
Support to Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, as the Ministry generates its own resources.
The Ministry is therefore exempted from making provisions for North East. As regards Ministry
of Social Justice and Empowerment, all Divisions of the Ministry other than the Scheduled Castes
Division (SCD) do earmark 10% of their Plan allocations to the North Eastern region. In the case
of the Scheduled Castes Division, only 2% of its GBS is allocated to the North East (NE),
considering the fact that the Scheduled Castes constitute less than 2% of the NE population.
8.4 The Committee in its reports on Demands for Grants for 2006-07 and 2007-08
recommended that the other Ministries may also be taken out from the List of Exempted Ministries/
Departments. The Ministry in its ATR on the recommendation of the Committee contained in its
127th Report stated as below:
“After a thorough review with the Ministries concerned, the exemption of Department of
Bio-technology has been withdrawn and some of the Ministries which have some scope
available for expenditure in the North Eastern Region were asked to provide maximum
possible percentage of GBS of the North Eastern Region. The Ministries which are
surrendering large sums of money have been requested to revise the norms according to the
conditions of North Eastern States so that they are able to utilize the money allocated in
the year of allocation.”

“The Ministry is in constant touch with other line Ministries and Departments to revise the

are yet to respond, the Ministries of Rural Development and Human Resource Development
have already changed the guidelines in favour of North Eastern States in respect of their

Ministries/Departments to change their norms according to the conditions of the NER have

integrated economic development in the eight North Eastern States and since 2002, it functions as
a regional planning body for its constituent states. Initially intended as an advisory body, the NEC’s

maintains security and public order. Where necessary it makes recommendations to the Centre for
further measures.

for the NER.

Terminals (ISTTs) in all State capitals;
(ii) Construction of lnter-State Roads and Roads of Economic Importance;

9.8 Explaining about the role of NEC, the Ministry in its written note stated as under:
“By the NEC (Amendment) Act, 2002, NEC has been mandated to function as a regional
advisory body. However, NEC has not been able to fulfill its role as a regional planning
body due to the large number of ongoing projects which could not be completed due to
financial constraints. The main emphasis is currently on completing the spill over projects.
It has, however, been decided that NEC should take only inter-state projects with wide
ranging impact and should focus on few areas of a critical nature and not spread its
resources thin. Projects of minor nature are not proposed to be taken up and substantive
projects more than Rs.2 crore each would be taken up. Many umbrella and subsidy-oriented
scheme like Scheme for Promotion of Industries in North East (SPINE), Sports and Youth
Affairs, Agriculture, etc. has been discontinued with a view to avoiding overlap with the
scheme launched by the Central Government and State Governments. NEC has also held
consultations with the State Governments in North Eastern Region to evolve a strategy for
developing a regional plan for development of the North Eastern Region. It has been
decided that the schemes of regional nature or with regional potential only would be taken
up. NEC will also take up projects which will supplement the State Governments projects
having inter-state potential. NEC is also proposing to initiate the exercise of dovetailing its
Annual Plans with the Annual Plans of the State Governments to take up project with wide-
ranging impact for the development of North Eastern Region. By taking up these exercises,
NEC will be able to function as a regional planning body whereby it can enforce its
authority on both line Ministries and the State Governments vis-a-vis in formulating,
allocating and evaluating schemes of a regional nature.”
9.9 The Ministry in its written reply has informed that the Planning Commission had agreed to
a projected outlay of Rs.3500 crore for the Tenth Plan but the total allocation made under this plan
was only Rs.2511.50 crore. Thus, there is a shortfall of Rs.988.50 crore in the tenth Plan

14
allocation. Due to this low allocation, various road projects approved during the ninth and tenth
Plans are still under construction.
9.10 The Committee takes a critical view of the allocations made for NEC. The allocation
of Rs.624 crore in BE 2008-09 as compared to the allocation of Rs.600 crore in the previous
year, is in no way commensurate with the number of projects to be taken up by NEC.
Besides the new projects, the NEC has also several spilled over projects. The Committee is
in agreement with the view that it is difficult for NEC to fulfill its role as a regional
planning body due to financial constraints. The Committee therefore recommends that the
NEC may be provided with suitably enhanced allocation at RE stage so that NEC projects
which are facing difficulties due to shortage of funds do not get affected.

States so as to facilitate regional integration and trade flows. The project also seeks to focus on
capacity building of state implementing agencies in the areas of road management, road safety,
environment and social assessment and an effective and efficient management of road assets.

15.0 PROMOTION OF TOURISM AND HOSPITALITY
15.1 The North Eastern Region of our country is known for its natural beauty in terms of exotic
flora and fauna which can be used as an attractive destination for eco and adventure tourism, but
the region has not been able to utilize its potential. Despite the flow of foreign tourists to India
having been increased by leaps and bounds during the last two-three years which has helped swell
foreign currency reserves of our country, the region has not been able to attract domestic as well
as foreign tourists. It is worth mentioning here that the region is infested with insurgents and the
basic infrastructure here is grossly inadequate.
15.2 In its Outcome Budget 2008-09, the Ministry has mentioned that the Tourism Sector was
introduced in the Tenth Plan only. The Tourism Sector has been supporting projects for
development of infrastructural facilities aiming at promotion of tourism in the region. For
introducing Public Private Partnership (PPP) model of development in the region, during the tenth
Plan money was provided to Infrastructure Leasing and Financial Services Ltd. (IL&FS) for
identifying locations, studying feasibility and bringing up of budget hotels in PPP model. So far four
projects. (one in Tripura and three in Assam) are in the pipeline and some others are also expected
to be finalized. In order to promote tourism, the sector has given priority to projects relating to
religious and cultural tourism, wild life tourism, adventure tourism, eco tourism, tea tourism, etc.
22

23

as travel handbooks, publicity through important national media, documentaries, etc. are also
supported.

Rs.501.00 lakh during 2007-08 and no change was proposed at the RE stage. However the

development in Assam and Arunachal Pradesh and one project for development of inland water

was organized at Gangtok on 27-28 April 2007;
(ii) A campaign to promote the North-East Region as a safe and attractive tourist
destination through electronic media;

by the Ministry on 16.01.2008;
(iv) A proposal for relaxing LTC Rules to provide incentives for Central Government
employees visiting the North-East Region;
(v) Funds were provided for skill upgradation in Tourism and Hospitality sector;
(vi) Promotion of Infrastructure through Government and PPP; and
(vii) The NEIIP 2007 has provided for incentives for the Hospitality Sector.

of interest from the private Sector for investment. In response to the query about private sector
participation in creating world class infrastructure to attract tourists, the Ministry has replied:
“The Ministry and the NEC are working with the Infrastructure Leasing and Finance
Limited (IL&FS) to develop tourism infrastructure in the North-East States. This
collaboration has led to commissioning of a Tata Group ‘Ginger’ hotel in Agartala. A
number of other projects are at different stages of development”.
15.7 In response to the query regarding initiatives taken by the Ministry under “Incredible India”
campaign, the Ministry mentioned as under:

24
“One of the reasons that has adversely affected the tourist and investment flow in the
region is the erroneous impression of the entire region being unsafe and ridden with
insurgency. This is in stark contrast with the fact that a large swathe of the region is among
the most peaceful parts of the country. The Ministry has launched a media compaign, which

“At present, the Ministry of Home Affairs is in dialogue with State Governments to relax

15.9 The Committee is of the considered view that the NE region has a great potential to
become an attractive tourist destination in the country particularly for eco and adventure
tourism. If the tourism potential of the region is to be fully tapped, sufficient infrastructure
and peaceful environment should be in place at the earliest. Moreover, tourism in NE
provides a large number of employment opportunities. The eco-tourism not only provides
livelihood for local communities and adds importance to local traditions and cultures, but
also generates substantial revenue for environmental conservation and management. The
Committee is pleased to note that in the proposed BE 2008-09, an amount of Rs.9 crore has

15.10 The Committee appreciates the several initiatives including Media Campaign and

infrastructure in the NER to make it one of the most attractive tourist destination not only
in the country but in the world as well. The Committee desires that a long-term perspective
plan and a roadmap may be prepared for creation of better tourism infrastructure on a fast
track basis as it is the main hurdle in the way of development of tourism sector in the
region.
15.11 The Committee desires that the Ministry in tandem with the Ministry of Home
Affairs and the Ministry of Tourism should expedite the issue of relaxing the movement of
tourists in the north-eastern region in the interest of development of NER and tourism.
16.0 CONNECTIVITY
16.1 The biggest problem being faced by the North Eastern Region in realizing its economic
potential is the problem of connectivity. The poor connectivity through road, rail, air and water has
been one of the biggest stumbling blocks in the way of the fast development of the region. It is
mainly due to hilly terrain in most of the North Eastern States and high cost of aircraft operation
in the region. The road connectivity in the North-east region is much below the national average
on most parameters. The Railway network in the north-eastern part of the country is far more

25
deficient than the required level which is only 4% of the country’s railway network. Even some
of the states have zero level of rail network. The intra region air connectivity as well as
connectivity with the rest of the country is of great concern from the point of view of
development of the region. In the northeast region and other remote areas, the management of
airport infrastructure as well as air services is not considered commercially viable because of low
utilization and low fare structures, etc. Given the topography and inaccessibility of the region, the
need for air services is much greater.
16.2 The Ministry in its Annual Report has mentioned that the Union Government’s intention is
to invest about Rs.50,000 crore on the road sector in the north-east region over the Eleventh Five
Year Plan period. The programmes include SARDP-NE, East-West Corridor, NHDP-II, PMGSY and
programmes initiated by Ministry of DoNER and NEC. Regarding railway network, it has been
decided that the projects of the Railways designated as National Projects will be supported by
Government of lndia in the ratio of 75:25 where 25% will be given from the GBS of Railways and
75% from Government of India. It has also been decided to create a Fund for development of rail
infrastructure in the North East. In the case of air-connectivity, greenfield Airports are proposed
to be developed at Itanagar, Cheithu and Pakyong and two new Greenfield airports have been
proposed at Tawang and Kokrajhar. Regarding inland water transport, renewal of lndo-Bangladesh
IWT protocol on long-term basis is being pursued and Kaladan River multi-modal transport route
from Mizoram to Sittwe port has been approved.
16.3 The most important organ of the Ministry of DoNER, i.e. NEC, spends around 40% of its
budget allocation on transport and communication. As per the Annual Report of the Ministry, during

the NEC. An agreement between NEC and Alliance Air was extended for the year 2008 for
operating ATR services between locations in the North East and NEC would pay Alliance Air
Rs. 38.5 crores as viability gap for operating the services.  The Airports  Authority of India (AAI)

16.10 ‘Connectivity’ within the NE region is of utmost importance if this region is to be
brought into the political, social and economic mainstream of the country. The Committee is of
the considered view that Government should adopt a proactive approach and should be diligent
in implementing the various policy initiatives. This area should be given topmost priority in the
scheme of governance of the NER and special impetus be provided wherever needed.
16.11 The Committee is satisfied that for BE 2008-09, an amount of Rs. 63845.00 lakh,
which is an increase of 58.02% over the last year, has been allocated for transport and
communication. The Committee is happy to note that the Union Government’s intention is

27
to invest an amount to the tune of Rs.50,000 crore on the road sector in the north-east
region over the eleventh plan period. The Committee is of the view that given the strategic
location of the region, the roads on the Indo-Myanmar border (under Special Accelerated
Road Development Programme for North East of DORTH), road to connect Mizoram and the
Kaladan Multi-modal project (under MEA), tri-lateral highway between India, Myanmar and
Thailand, important roads in Myanmar (Tamu Kalewa road, Rih Tidim and Rih Falam roads)
should be upgraded/constructed at a fast pace and completed at the earliest.
16.12 The Committee recommends that development of proposed three Greenfield airports
at Itanagar, Cheithu and Pakyong should be given priority. The Committee desires that the
proposal regarding two new greenfield airports at Tawang and Kokrajhar be examined
expeditiously. The Committee is pleased to know that the agreement between NEC and
Alliance Air has been extended for the year 2008 for operating ATR services between
locations in the North East. The Committee desires that airports at Silchar, Dibrugarh and
Umroi may also be upgraded at the earliest. It should be impressed upon the AAI to submit
its DPR on non operational airports, namely, Kailashahar, Kamalpur and Pasighat and DPR
on Tezu airport, as early as possible.
16.13 Regarding inland water transport, the Committee recommends that Indo-Bangladesh
IWT Protocol and Kaladan River multi-modal transport route from Mizoram to Sittwe Port
should be given utmost importance as they could help increase foreign trade with
neighbouring countries.
17.0 ROPEWAY AT TAWANG
17.1 The Committee recalls that the foundation for the Ropeway was laid by the President of
India way back in 2002. Funds had been released for Tawang Ropeway in July 2006. The
Committee in its 120th Report on Demands for Grants (2006-07) expressed its dismay over the
inordinate delay in the matter. The Committee in its 127th Report on Demands for Grants
(2007-08) recommended as under:
“Now, that the funds have been released and work has already commenced, the Committee
urged upon the Ministry to ensure that the work is finished as per the target fixed”.
17.2 The Ministry in its Action Taken Notes on the above recommendation replied as under:
“The State Government was implementing the projects and funds have been released and
they have been requested to implement in a time bound manner as per the fixed target”.
17.3 During the oral evidence before the Committee, when it was pointed out that the project
of Ropeway from Tawang Monastery to Ani Gompa at Lawagn of Arunachal Pradesh was still not
progressing satisfactorily, the Secretary informed as under:—
“After the sanction, we have already released Rs.1.04 crore as the first instalment to the
State Government on 19.7.06, and the Government of Arunachal Pradesh is implementing
it. The information is that the State Government was in the process of issuing tenders in
August, 2007”.
17.4 The Ropeway project at Tawang is a classic example of procrastination. The
Committee expresses its displeasure over the fact that the foundation for the Ropeway was
laid by the President of India in 2002 yet the progress of construction of this ropeway is
not at all satisfactory. Even though funds were allocated last year, it is a matter of concern
that the State Government was in the process of issuing tenders in August 2007. It is
unfortunate that the Secretary could not give the latest status of the project. The
Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the Ministry must take suitable initiatives

28
and follow-up action to ensure completion of project without further delay. Otherwise, the
Committee apprehends that there would be time and cost overruns.

on their substantial expansion. The incentives include income tax and excise exemption, capital
investment subsidy, interest subsidy, insurance subsidy, and transport subsidy are applicable to
industrial units set up in the NER, regardless of their location.

18.3 The Ministry of DoNER in its written reply has explained the salient features of this new
industrial policy which are as follows:—
(i) NEIIPP covers all eight States of the North Eastern Region including Sikkim;
(ii) All new units and existing units going in for substantial expansion and which
commence commercial production within 10 years i.e. upto March, 2016 will be
eligible under NEIIPP for incentives;
(iii) Incentives to be available to all industrial units, new and existing ones, on their
substantial expansion located anywhere in the region;
(iv) Incentives on substantial expansion would be given to units affecting an increase by
minimum 25% in the value of its fixed capital investment in plant and machinery;
(v) 100% excise duty exemption on finished products made in the North Eastern Region;
(vi) 100% income tax exemption is available under NEIIPP;
(vii) Capital Investment Subsidy upto 30% of investment in plant and machinery
is available under the Policy. The limit for automatic approval of subsidy is
Rs.1.5 crores/unit. Such subsidy is applicable to units in private sector, joint sector,
cooperative sector as well as units set up by the State Government of the North
Eastern Region;
(viii) Interest subsidy is available @ 3% on working capital;
(ix) New and industrial units on substantial expansion are eligible for reimbursement of
100% of insurance premium;
(x) The NEIIPP, 2007 has a very small negative list comprising of goods such as
tobacco, manufactured tobacco substitute, pan masala, plastic carry bag of less than
twenty microns, goods produced by petroleum oil or gas refinery;
18.4 The Committee was further apprised of the following incentives available to service sector
industries under NEIIPP:—
(i) Hotels (not below Two Star category), adventure and leisure sports including
ropeways;
(ii) M edical and health services in the nature of nursing homes with a minimum capacity
of 25 beds and old-age homes;
(iii) V ocational training institutes such as institutes for hotel management, catering and
food crafts, entrepreneurship development, nursing and para medical, civil aviation
related training, fashion, design and industrial training;
(iv) Bio-technology industries will be eligible as any other industry under the Policy;
(v) Power generating plants will continue to get incentives as governed under Section
81A of the Income Tax Act. Also power generating plants upto 10 MW based on both
conventional and non-conventional sources will be eligible for capital investment
subsidy, interest subsidy and comprehensive insurance under NEIIPP, 2007;
(vi) Number of tax concessions under Sections l0A and 10AA of the Income Tax Act are
available to the IT sector. However, in the North East, non-availability of trained
human resource is a constraining factor for development of the IT sector. Hence, tax
benefits under Section 80 IC of Income Tax Act will be extended to IT related
training centres and IT hardware units.

30
18.5 The North East Industrial and Investment Promotion Policy (NEIIPP), 2007 seeks to
emphasize on the sunrise sector of the economy which complements well with the strengths and
requirements of development of the North Eastern region. Emphasis on promoting hospitality
industry has been made in view of the vast scope for tourism in the region which is yet untapped.
Due to fragile ecological nature of the region, there is a need to promote non-polluting industries.
Hence, the policy emphasizes that incentives will be available to bio-technology, IT and ITES, small
hydel projects both conventional and non-conventional, health institutions. In keeping with the rich
textile tradition of the region, fashion and design are also covered under the services sector for
incentives.
18.6 The Ministry further added that the 3rd North East Business Summit was held on
10-11 April, 2007 in Delhi to promote the North East as an investment destination. It was well
attended by investors. Seminars included technical sessions on Investments and incentives,
infrastructure, Agro and Food Processing, Tourism, etc. and as a result of the Summit, 128
expressions of interest were received from entrepreneurs for investment in the North East Region.
18.7 Despite the North-East Region being rich in natural resources, it is one of the most
industrially backward regions of the country. Poor transport infrastructure, inaccessibility to sea,
and inadequate infrastructure for harnessing the available natural resources, geographical
remoteness from the economic mainstream of our country and insurgency are the main hurdles in
the way of the development of a sustainable industrial base in the region. The region also borders
some neighboring countries but it still has not realized its potential in international trade and
investment.
18.8 The Committee is pleased to note that several incentives have been taken for new
industrial units as well as the existing ones in the NEIIPP, 2007. While appreciating the
initiatives to attract foreign investment in the region, the Committee feels that more
emphasis should be given on potential investors from other parts of India. However, in
order to give fillip to the NEIIPP, 2007, the Committee recommends that the Ministry of
DoNER should interact with the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises for
promoting enterprises including Agro and rural industries. The Committee strongly feels
that the benefits accruing from Micro Small Medium Enterprises Act, 2005. Khadi and
Village Industries Corporation Act 2007, North East Industrial and Investment Promotion
Policy 2007 would go a long way in promoting MSMEs in the region provided adequate
institutional arrangement and proper awareness are in place. The Committee also
recommends that the Government should give high priority to the problem of connectivity
in the region as without proper and adequate connectivity the investors would not be
convinced for investing in the region.
19.0 INITIATIVES UNDER INDIA’S LOOK EAST POLICY
19.1 The geo-st rategic location of the North-East makes the region significant for India’s
growing economic ties with the countries of South-East Asia. The Region has common frontiers
with Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar and Tibetan Autonomous Region. The Committee has
been given to understand that the Union Minister for External Affairs held a meeting on 31.10.2007
with the Chief Ministers of the North-East States and Central Ministries concerned to formulate a
strategy for a meaningful involvement of the North-East Region in the Look East Policy. The other
important developments in this regard include resumption of Indo-China trade at Nathula Pass in
Sikkim and progress on Kaladan multi-modal route through Mizoram to Sittwe port which provides
an alternative to transit through Bangladesh.
19.2 The Ministry in its written reply has stated that to facilitate trade and commerce in the
Region and promote the North East as a trade hub, it had organized a “North East India Trade and

31
Investment Opportunities Week” in Bangkok in October, 2007. This event evinced keen interest
among Indian and Thai businessmen and entrepreneurs in sectors such as Agriculture, Food
Processing, Hydro-electricity, Dams, Inland water transport, Road construction, Tourism and
Hospitality. This event at Bangkok was followed with the visit of the Thai delegation led by the
Deputy Minister of Industry, comprising both Thai public and private sectors, to the three states
of the NE region viz; Sikkim, Assam and Arunachal during January 9-12th,  2008 to zero in the
areas of trade and investment cooperation between the two countries. The Ministry further
informed that there was an ongoing initiative with NRIs of North East Region in the United States.
Encouraged by the receptiveness of the Summit at Bangkok, discussions are being initiated with
Australia, Singapore, ASEAN and UAE to spur their business interests in the North East. Ministry
has also taken initiative to project NE Region as an attractive FDI and trade destination with the
development of key infrastructure sectors, under the Look East Policy and through North East
Industrial and Investment Promotion Policy.
19.3 During the oral evidence before the Committee, the Secretary stated as under
“...After the Look East policy was announced with involvement of State Chief Ministers
and several Ministries, action points concerning all the Ministries were drawn up, and,
these were, particularly, roads, transport and others. .....I have personally had meetings with
Secretary (Commerce) and we have come to an agr eement with regard to the area that need
to be focussed upon for strengthening infrastructure. As far as “Moreh” is concerned, States
are being asked to increase the number of items that can be traded from across the border.
.....Strengthening of border trade is receiving the highest attention. Improving the
infrastructure of Land Customs Stations for the border trade also needs to be done.”
19.4 The Committee recognizes that under India’s Look East Policy, border trade with
neighboring landlocked countries is of utmost importance as the North East Region
could provide a link between India and South East Asian countries for increasing
trade between the two regions. The Committee therefore recommends that the ‘Look
East Policy’ may be followed up vigorously in close coordination with other concerned
Union Ministries and State Governments. As pointed out by the Secretary Ministry
of DoNER the infrastructure of the Land Customs Stations needs to be improved for
better border trade.
20.0 VISION NER 2020
20.1 The Ministry of DoNER and NEC are in the process of preparing a Vision NER 2020
document reflecting the aspirations of the people of the region for a holistic and comprehensive
development of the region in which the fruits of the growth of the Indian economy will extend
to the people of the North East.
20.2 When asked about the status of the formulation of vision NER 2020, the Ministry in its
written reply maintained
“National Institute of Public Finance and Policy had prepared a three-volume Vision
Document. The Document was scrutinized in public hearings held in 12 cities of the North
East in 2007. At present, the Document is being given final touches. It is expected to be
adopted by the NEC in its next Plenary meeting to be held in the summer of 2008. Wide
publicity will be given as and when the Document is finally adopted.”
20.3 The Committee desires that Vision NER 2020 should be formulated at the earliest for
overall development of the region. The Committee feels that the schemes for development
of transport infrastructure, industrial base, agricultural and allied sectors with special
emphasis on medicinal plants in the region should be given prominence in the Vision NER
2020. The Committee hopes that the Vision document would give a direction to the

32
development process in the region. The Committee recommends that the Government
should strictly adhere to the schedule of adoption of this Vision Document.
21.0 POWER SECTOR
21.1 Hydro Power in the North Eastern Region constitutes the most important resource of the
region due to availability of large number of water bodies. Given this easily available natural
resource of water, the region has the potential to become ‘powerhouse’ of the country which could
cater to the needs of the region as well as the other parts of lndia. But, still this potential of the
region has remained untapped.
21.2 Replying to the Committee’s query regarding development of Hydro Power Projects in the
region, the Ministry’s stated as under:—
“In the area of Hydro power, few new projects have been taken up but the thrust is on
completion of ongoing projects and the Small Hydropower Projects (a new initiative taken
up during the 11th Five Year Plan). The Power Sector was allocated 10.83% of the
2007-08 Budget allocation. New transmission/ sub-transmission lines and system
improvement, Small Hydro Projects, Support for conduct of Load Flow Study through CEA
and Viability gap funding for new and renewable energy schemes are proposed to be
undertaken during 11th Plan.”
21.3 During the oral evidence before the Committee, the Secretary stated as under:
“In the field of power also, certain initiatives have been taken. In fact, a summit on power
was held last year. ... there were several initiatives which were highlighted during that time.
Several commitments were given by the Ministry of Power as to how they could intervene
for setting up more projects. The Dibang project has already been inaugurated by the hon.
Prime Minister in his recent visit. Then, there is also very great emphasis on the smaller
micro-hydel projects, as they are called .....NEC itself is implementing so many of them and
also on non-conventional energy sources.”
21.4 During the oral evidence before the Committee, while complementing the reply of the
Secretary, DoNER, the Chief Engineer (CEA) added
“...In the Eleventh Plan, we will be commissioning nine projects with a total capacity
of 4055 MW. .....out of 4055 MW, 3110 MW is in the Central sector. That means 75 per
cent of the projects that are going to come in the Eleventh Plan are in the Central Sector.
Other projects are in the State sector and in the private sector.”
21.5 The Committee has also noted that the first sectoral summit of NEC held on
16-17 January, 2007 dealt with power sector. The following recommendations were made in the
summit:
“A two pronged strategy to be adopted for power generation with focus on Small/Localised
Hydel and Thermal and NRE projects for catering to local needs and High capacity Hydel
and Thermal Power Projects with associated Transmission lines for first meeting the demand
for power of the North Eastern Region and thereafter that of the rest of the country.
Ministry of Power to develop a clear, coherent and sustainable Power Policy for the NER
taking into account the special characteristics and needs of the Region.
CEA to undertake feasibility studies for utilizing considerable shale deposits in Arunachal
Pradesh and coal deposits in Assam and Meghalaya with the objective of increasing the
share of thermal power.

33
PGCIL to invest more in the trunk transmission lines for improving inter and intra-region
connectivity. Priority to be accorded for creating a grid to meet power shortages in the
North Eastern States.
Transmission, sub-transmission and distribution system improvement to be one of the thrust
areas for NEC during Elevenh Plan.
State Governments to prepare perspective plans for Transmission, sub-transmission and
Distribution Systems in their respective States to cover the Eleventh Plan period (2007-12).
The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas to accord due consideration to the suggestions

The issue of high transmission charges, presently under reference to CERC, needs to be

On the basis of the reports of the 4 sub-groups, a Master Plan for Power Development in

21.6 The Committee is of the view that there is an immense potential of hydro-power in

21.7 The Committee also recommends that the Ministry of DoNER may examine the
recommendations made in the Sectoral Summit held in January, 2007, in collaboration with
other concerned ministries and take a view on each of the recommendations at the earliest.

OBSERV ATIONS/CONCLUSIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS — AT A GLANCE
OVERALL ASSESSMENT OF THE DEMANDS FOR GRANTS
The Committee is concerned that even though the Ministry of DoNER made a
projection of Rs.2922 crore for the current year, the actual allocation made was Rs.1455
crore under plan scheme. The Committee has been given to understand that due to the
reduction in the allocation by almost 50%, many projects would suffer. The Ministry will not
be able to implement the schemes for the development of the region. The Committee,
therefore, strongly recommends that the allocation to the Ministry be made as per its
requirement as it would be in the interest of the overall development of the North-East
Region. (Para 7.5)
The Committee is not convinced by the reasoning given by the Secretary, NEC on the
visibility aspect of the development. The component of private investment is a totally
different matter to be viewed in the proper context and perspective. First of all, the
outcome of the public investments should be visible and transparent. Then only a positive
message will go for private investment. The Committee appreciates that there are basic and
inherent problems in converting public investment into tangible results. That can only be
achieved if there is a sense of commitment among implementing agencies and the State
Governments. The Committee recommends that sincere efforts should be made to ensure
that whatever investment is made for the development of NER should yield concrete result
so much so that the outcome should manifest itself. (Para 7.6)
NON-LAPSABLE CENTRAL POOL OF RESOURCES (NLCPR)
The Committee feels that the efforts made by Ministry of DoNER to persuade
Ministries/Departments to change their norms according to the conditions of the NER have
not yielded the desired results. The Committee recommends that more vigorous efforts
need to be made by the Ministry of DoNER so that more and more Ministries/Departments
change their norms in respect of their flagship programmes and spend the allocated amount
in the NER. (Para 8.6)
The Committee views with concern the fact that even though DoNER had projected
Rs. 1200 crore for NLCPR, only Rs. 650 crore has been allocated for the current financial
year. The Committee also takes note of the fact that for NLCPR the projection was made
on the basis of performance during the last two years. The Committee further notes the
unspent balance lying with other Ministries. The Committee therefore recommends that the
allocation for NLCPR may be increased appropriately at RE stage to meet the requirement
of various projects proposed to be taken up by the Ministry. The Committee also
recommends that allocation may also be made from out of the unspent balance of various
Ministries. The Committee desires that the Ministry of DoNER may pursue the matter at
highest level for early release of the funds. (Para 8.13)
The Committee is constrained to observe that the State Governments could not
complete 233 projects within the time schedule mainly due to the delays in utilization of
funds and limited working seasons. The Committee is however not convinced by the reasons
35

36
for the backlog in completion of projects. The Committee strongly recommends that the
State Governments should strictly adhere to the time schedule in this regard. (Para 8.14)
NORTH-EASTERN COUNCIL
The Committee takes a critical view of the allocations made for NEC. The allocation
of Rs. 624 crore in BE 2008-09 as compared to the allocation of Rs. 600 crore in the
previous year, is in no way commensurate with the number of projects to be taken up by
NEC. Besides the new projects, the NEC has also several spilled over projects. The
Committee is in agreement with the view that it is difficult for NEC to fulfill its role as
a regional planning body due to financial constraints. The Committee therefore recommends
that the NEC may be provided with suitably enhanced allocation at RE stage so that
NEC projects which are facing difficulties due to shortage of funds do not get affected.
(Para 9.10)
ADVOCACY AND PUBLICITY
The Committee takes note of the reply given by the Ministry that media campaign
will be operational soon. The Committee would like to be apprised of the activities to be
undertaken under the media plan. The Committee recommends that efforts should be made
to achieve the objectives of the strategy in right earnest. The Committee is also of the view
that whatever steps that are being taken under ‘Advocacy and Publicity’ and its results are
still not visible. It feels that there must be inherent weaknesses and problems in the plans
being made. In the present age of globlisation, efforts should be made to bring the North-
East Region into the mainstream of the country at the earliest and for that Advocacy and
Publicity is the most effective medium. The Committee therefore recommends that renewed
thrust may be given on media campaign and it should be effectively used. (Para 10.9)
TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AND CAPACITY BUILDING
The Committee is happy to note that 36 students have been selected for training in
Commercial Pilot Licence (CPL) and Air craft Maintenance Engineering (AME) and some
young persons have also been selected for airhostess training. The Committee however,
wishes to observe that these trainings are being held outside the North-Eastern region. If
the North-Eastern region has to be strengthened and the capacity for the region has to be
upgraded, such Institutes should be opened there instead of sending people outside for
training. The Committee, therefore, recommends that an early decision may be taken on
starting the Pilot Training Institute at Lilabari. Whatever problems that are coming in the
way be sorted out at the earliest and the Central Ministry may take initiative in this
regard. The Committee is of the view that there is huge potential for fashion designing and
fashion technology in the North East which is still to be tapped. The Committee reiterates
that a National Institute of Fashion Technology may be opened in the North East at the
earliest. The Committee is also of the view that there is a huge potential for sports persons
in the North East and this potential has not yet been tapped. To tap this potential, a
separate Sports Institute or Sports Academy is required in the North East. The Committee,
therefore, reiterates that a Sports Academy may be opened in the North Eastern Region.
(Para 11.7)
EXTERNALLY AIDED PROJECTS
The North East States Roads Projects (NESRP) is an important ADB assisted project.
With the implementation of this project, road connectivity in the North-east region will

37
improve significantly. The Committee, therefore, desir es that EFC/CCEA approval for the
project may be obtained at the earliest. The Committee feels that the project must take off
during 2008-09 and there should not be any delay in this regard. The Committee
recommends that follow up action on the report of the consultants on North Eastern States
Trade Investment Creation Initiative Project (NESTICI) may be taken immediately. Efforts
should be made to ensure that the implementation of the project commences during the
current year. The Committee observes that even though NER Livelihood Project (NERLP)
scheme was approved in September 2006, the project is still at the stage of selection of
consultants for preparing the main project reports. The project is taking a very long time
to take off and by the time it is implemented, there will be cost overrun which may
necessitate a review. The Committee therefore recommends that all out efforts should be
made to ensure that NERLP is implemented during 2008-09. (Para 12.10)
NORTH EASTERN REGIONAL AGRICULTURAL MARKETING CORPORATION LTD. (NERAMAC)
The Committee recognizes the fact that the North East Region, though industrially
backward due to poor infrastructure, has great potential in terms of agriculture,
horticulture, floriculture. This potential of the region has remained unharnessed and here
the NERAMAC comes into the picture which could accelerate the growth in these sectors.
The Committee expresses its disquiet over the fact that the Ministry in general and
NERAMAC in particular are not able to tap the potential available in abundance and this
shows poor planning and initiative. Sincere efforts are required to be made to harness these
resources. The Committee recommends that the pineapple juice concentrate plant in Tripura
may be revived by providing it better machineries and skilled manpower. (Para 13.8)
TRANSFER OF HILL AREA DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME (HADP) AND BORDER AREA
DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME (BADP)
The Committee expresses its deep concern that even though the two programmes
i.e., Hill Area Development Programme (HADP) and Border Area Development Programme
(BADP) are shown in the Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961 against
the Ministry of DoNER but the programmes are yet to be transferred to it. The Committee
is constrained to note that inspite of its recommendation in the One Hundred and Twenty
Seventh report, the Cabinet Secretariat has not taken any steps in this direction. The issue
is pending with that Secretariat since long. The Committee reiterates that such important
issue should be resolved on priority basis. (Para 14.4)
PROMOTION OF TOURISM AND HOSPITALITY
The Committee is of the considered view that the NE region has a great potential to
become an attractive tourist destination in the country particularly for eco and adventure
tourism. If the tourism potential of the region is to be fully tapped, sufficient infrastructure
and peaceful environment should be in place at the earliest. Moreover, tourism in NE
provides a large number of employment opportunities. The eco-tourism not only provides
livelihood for local communities and adds importance to local traditions and cultures,
but also generates substantial revenue for environmental conservation and management.
The Committee is pleased to note that in the proposed BE 2008-09, an amount of
Rs.9 crore has been allocated for Tourism which is an increase of 79.64% from the last
year. (Para 15.9)
The Committee appreciates the several initiatives including Media Campaign and
involving the private sector for development of the tourism sector, taken by the Ministry.

38
However, a lot more is yet to be done and a lot of investment is required to develop tourist
infrastructure in the NER to make it one of the most attractive tourist destination not only
in the country but in the world as well. The Committee desires that a long-term perspective
plan and a roadmap may be prepared for creation of better tourism infrastructure on a  fast
track basis as it is the main hurdle in the way of development of tourism sector in the
region. (Para 15.10)
The Committee desires that the Ministry in tandem with the Ministry of Home
Affairs and the Ministry of Tourism should expedite the issue of relaxing the movement of
tourists in the north-eastern region in the interest of development of NER and tourism.
(Para 15.11)
CONNECTIVITY
‘Connectivity’ within the NE region is of utmost importance if this region is to be
brought into the political, social and economic mainstr eam of the country. The Committee
is of the considered view that Government should adopt a proactive approach and should be
diligent in implementing the various policy initiatives. This area should be given topmost
priority in the scheme of governance of the NER and special impetus be provided wherever
needed. (Para 16.10)
The Committee is satisfied that for BE 2008-09, an amount of Rs.63845.00 lakh,
which is an increase of 58.02% over the last year, has been allocated for transport and
communication. The Committee is happy to note that the Union Government’s intention is
to invest an amount to the tune of Rs. 50,000 crore on the road sector in the north-east
region over the eleventh plan period. The Committee is of the view that given the strategic
location of the region, the roads on the Indo-Myanmar border (under Special Accelerated
Road Development Programme for North East of DORTH), road to connect Mizoram and the
Kaladan Multi-modal project (under MEA), tri-lateral highway between India, Myanmar and
Thailand, important roads in Myanmar (Tamu Kalewa road, Rih Tidim and Rih Falam roads)
should be upgraded/constructed at a fast pace and completed at the earliest. (Para 16.11)
The Committee recommends that development of proposed three Greenfield airports
at Itanagar, Cheithu and Pakyong should be given priority. The Committee desires that the
proposal regarding two new greenfield airports at Tawang and Kokrajhar be examined
expeditiously. The Committee is pleased to know that the agreement between NEC and
Alliance Air has been extended for the year 2008 for operating ATR services between
locations in the North East. The Committee desires that airports at Silchar, Dibrugarh and
Umroi may also be upgraded at the earliest. It should be impressed upon the AAI to submit
its DPR on non operational airports, namely, Kailashahar, Kamalpur and Pasighat and DPR
on Tezu airport, as early as possible. (Para 16.12)
Regarding inland water transport, the Committee recommends that Indo-Bangladesh
IWT Protocol and Kaladan River multi-modal transport route from Mizoram to Sittwe Port
should be given utmost importance as they could help increase foreign trade with
neighbouring countries. (Para 16.13)
ROPEWAY AT TAWANG
The Ropeway project at Tawang is a classic example of procrastination. The
Committee expresses its displeasure over the fact that the foundation for the Ropeway was
laid by the President of India in 2002 yet the progress of construction of this ropeway is
not at all satisfactory. Even though funds were allocated last year, it is a matter of concern

39
that the State Government was in the process of issuing tenders in August 2007. It is
unfortunate that the Secretary could not give the latest status of the project. The
Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the Ministry must take suitable initiatives
and follow-up action to ensure completion of project without further delay. Otherwise, the
Committee apprehends that there would be time and cost overruns. (Para 17.4)
NORTH EAST INDUSTRIAL AND INVESTMENT PROMOTION POLICY  (NEIIPP) 2007
The Committee is pleased to note that several incentives have been taken for new
industrial units as well as the existing ones in the NEIIP, 2007. While appreciating the
initiatives to attract foreign investment in the region, the Committee feels that more
emphasis should be given on potential investors from other parts of India. However, in
order to give fillip to the NEIIPP 2007, the Committee recommends that the Ministry of
DoNER should interact with the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises for
promoting enterprises including Agro and rural industries. The Committee strongly feels
that the benefits accruing from Micro Small Medium Enterprises Act, 2005. Khadi and
Village Industries Corporation Act, 2007, North East Industrial and Investment Promotion
Policy 2007 would go a long way in promoting MSMEs in the region provided adequate
institutional arrangement and proper awareness are in place. The Committee also
recommends that the Government should give high priority to the problem of connectivity
in the region as without proper and adequate connectivity the investors would not be
convinced for investing in the region. (Para 18.8)
INITIATIVES UNDER INDIA’S LOOK EAST POLICY
The Committee recognizes that under India’s Look East Policy, border trade with
neighboring landlocked countries is of utmost importance as the North East Region could
provide a link between India and South East Asian countries for increasing trade between
the two regions. The Committee therefore recommends that the ‘Look East Policy’ may be
followed up vigorously in close coordination with other concerned Union Ministries and State
Governments. As pointed out by the Secretary Ministry of DoNER the infrastructure of the
Land Customs Stations needs to be improved for better border trade. (Para 19.4)
VISION NER 2020
The Committee desires that Vision NER 2020 should be formulated at the earliest for
overall development of the region. The Committee feels that the schemes for development
of transport infrastructure, industrial base, agricultural and allied sectors with special
emphasis on medicinal plants in the region should be given prominence in the Vision NER
2020. The Committee hopes that the Vision document would give a direction to the
development process in the region. The Committee recommends that the Government
should strictly adhere to the schedule of adoption of this Vision Document. (Para 20.3)
POWER SECTOR
The Committee is of the view that there is an immense potential of hydro-power in
the region which has still not been fully harnessed. The Committee recommends that the
emphasis should be laid on completion of on-going projects without further delay before new
projects are taken up in the Eleventh Plan. (Para 21.6)
The Committee also recommends that the Ministry of DoNER may examine the
recommendations made in the Sectoral Summit held in January, 2007, in collaboration

40
with other concerned ministries and take a view on each of the recommendations at the
earliest. (Para 21.7)
EDUCATION
The Committee feels that there is some mismatch in the figures pertaining to
literacy and dropout rates in the NE States. The Committee therefore recommends that the
figures should be re-checked/verified by the concerned authorities so as to get the true
picture in this regard. Regarding shortage of teachers in NE States, the Committee
recommends that the Two Years’ Certificate course in Teachers’ Training offered by IGNOU
through the distance learning mode, may be availed of effectively for training of existing
teachers. At the same time setting up of new teacher training institutes may also be
considered. The Committee is optimistic that the revised funding pattern of 90:10 will give
a boost to Sarva Shiksha Abiyan in the NE Region. (Para 22.5)

PREFACE
I, the Chairperson of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home
Affairs, having been authorized by the Committee to submit the Report on its behalf, do hereby
present this One Hundred and Thirty-fourth Report on the Foreign Contribution (Regulation)
Bill, 2006 (Annexure I) .
2. In pursuance of the rules relating to the Department-related Parliamentary Standing
Committees, the Chairman, Rajya Sabha, referred* the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Bill, 2006,
as introduced in the Rajya Sabha on 18 December 2006 and pending therein, to the Committee for
examination and report within three months. Due to preoccupation of the Committee with other
urgent and pressing work relating to Bills and legislative business, extension of time upto the last
week of the Monsoon Session (2007) was initially granted by the Chairman, Rajya Sabha, for
presentation of the Report. Further extensions were granted by the Chairman, the last being upto
the first week of the Monsoon Session, 2008.
3. The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Bill, 2006 has been brought to consolidate the law to
regulate the acceptance and utilization of foreign contribution or foreign hospitality by certain
individuals or associations or companies and to prohibit acceptance and utilization of foreign
contribution or foreign hospitality for any activities detrimental to the national interest and for
matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. The Bill also seeks to repeal the present Act,
namely, The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 1976.
4. The Committee issued a Press Communique  (Annexure II)  on the Bill on 9th February
2007 inviting views/suggestions on the Bill. In response thereof, a large number of memoranda
were received. After scrutiny, 52 memoranda were found relevant and forwarded to the Ministry
of Home Affairs for their comments. The Committee also sought views/suggestions of various
political parties on the Bill and received the same from six political parties (Annexure IV) .
5. The Committee in its meeting held on 12th June, 2007, heard the presentation of the Home
Secretary, Government of India on the Bill and held preliminary discussion thereon. The Committee
in its meeting held on 20th June 2007 decided to hear non-official witnesses including
representatives of RBI, SBI, ICICI and HDFC Banks as well as some NGOs on the Bill.
5.1 In its sittings held on 16th and 17th July, and 3rd October 2007, the Committee heard the
views of Dr. Bimal Jalan, Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha and ex-Governor, RBI and
representatives of the following organizations on the Bill:
(i) Reserve Bank of India;
(ii) State Bank of India;
(iii) ICICI Bank;
(iv) HDFC Bank;
(v) Catholic Bishop’s Conference of India;
(vi) National Council of Churches in India;

(viii) Representatives of V oluntary Action Network India; and
(ix) Institute of Chartered Accountants of India.
5.2 The Committee in its sitting held on 6th November, 2007 and 9th January, 2008 heard the
representatives of Planning Commission on the compatibility of the Bill vis-a-vis National Policy on
V oluntary Sector, a policy document of V oluntary Sector Cell, Planning Commission, Government
