of some of the projects in consultation w ith the subject matter Ministries and reputed 
institutes, which NE States can use for implementation. 
 
Further Recommendation: 
3.7.3 The Committee takes a serious view of the delay at several levels in putting in 
place a robust monitoring mechanism for ensuri ng timely completion of the projects in 
the NER.  The Committee notes that the various  steps mooted by the Ministry are still 
at proposal stage only.  The Committee woul d, therefore, like to be informed of the 
status of implementation of the various monitoring mechanisms and concrete results 
achieved due to the monitoring systems already in force.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 28

CHAPTER- IV 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH FINAL 
REPLIES OF THE GOVERNMENT HAVE NOT BEEN RECEIVED 
 
4.1 BODOLAND TERRITORIAL COUNCIL (BTC) 
 
Recommendation 
4.1.1 The Committee notes the above information.  The Committee desires that the 
remaining twenty five projects should be co mpleted without further delay.  Though financial 
allocation had commenced in 2004-05 and the commitment of a ssistance was completed in 
2008-09 and allocation is still cont inuing, it is unfortunate that the physical targets have not 
been achieved so far.  If it continues like this, the very purpose of financial assistance would 
be defeated. The Committee recommends that the balance amount of Rs. 36.37 crore out of 
the sanctioned amount, may be released at the ear liest so that the projects may be completed 
as per schedule in a time bound manner.   
 (Para 2.5.6) 
Action Taken  
4.1.2 It is a fact that 42 projects with appr oved / indicative cost of Rs. 476.26 crore has 
been sanctioned as per the Memorandum of Settlement (MoS) signed between Govt. of India 
and Bodo Liberation Tigers (BLT) in the year 2003 wherein it was agreed to provide 
financial assistance of Rs. 100 crore per annum for 5 years (Rs. 500 crores) for projects to 
develop the socio – economic infrastructure in Bodo Territorial Council (BTC) areas over 
and above the normal plan assistance to the St ate of Assam. Agains t the total approved / 
indicative cost of Rs. 476.26 crore, Rs. 450.50 crore has so far been released by this Ministry 
against which the State Government have sent  the UC for Rs. 352.57 crore.  (The figure of 
releases includes Rs.10.61 crore released during 2010-11). The State Government have 
submitted the Completion Certificates (CCs) for 17 Projects.  
 
4.1.3 The matter regarding non – utilization of funds and non – completion of the projects 
after lapse of more than 4 years have been regularly followed – up with the Government of 
Assam / BTC but the desired result could no t be achieved. The matter relating to the 
completion of remaining 25 projects will natu rally be vigorously followed up with the State 
Government / BTC.  
 
4.1.4 So far as releasing the balance amount of  36.37 crore is concerned, Rs. 10.61 crore, as 
shown above, has been released  in the current financial ye ar i.e. 2010 -1 1 (till 10.11.2010) 
and the remaining amount of Rs . 25.76 crore will be released on receipt of all necessary 
documents such as UC, QPR, Inspection Report, Work Plan, Photographs and Reasons for 
delay etc.  
 
Further Recommendation 
4.1.5 The Committee is constrained to express it s displeasure over the fact that despite 
vigorous follow-up action by Ministry of DoNER, the projects could not be completed in 
time.  The Committee recommends that all th e projects should be completed and the 
funds allocated should be utilized on with in a strict timeframe. The Committee notes 
that the Government has still not released th e balance of the sanctioned amount for the 
year 2009-10.   The Committee hopes that the Ministry of DONER would play an active 
 29

role in procuring all the necessary docume nts viz. UC, QPR, Inspection Report, Work 
Plan, etc. for timely release of funds so  that the pending projects are completed 
expeditiously.  
 
4.2 CONNECTIVITY 
 
Recommendation: 
4.2.1 The Committee feels that development of infras tructure in the civil aviation sector has 
been hit by bottlenecks mainly on account of  land acquisition and environmental issues. In 
this context, the Committee woul d like to suggest that a Master Plan for creation of civil 
aviation facilities in NE Region on the lines of the Road Development Plan namely SARDP-
NE may be prepared. In this connection, the Committee would like to mention that in its One 
Hundred and Thirty-third and One Hundred and Forty-first reports, it had recommended for 
completion of upgradation of the airports with out further delay. The Committee, reiterating 
its earlier recommendations, desires that all necessary steps may be taken for development of 
existing airports and upgradation and operationalisation of non-operational airports in the 
NER within a strict time schedule.  
(Para 3.3.17) 
Action Taken: 
4.2.2 The para has been referred to the Mini stry of Civil Aviation for seeking their 
comments and the same are awaited. 
4.2.3 The responsibility of development of airpor ts and air connectivity rests with Ministry 
of Civil Aviation. However, NEC has supported the development of the Airports in the NER. 
The issue of Master Plan on the lines of SARD P-NE was raised in the meeting held in the 
Ministry of Civil Aviation on a number of occasions. The issue was reiterated by the 
Secretary, DoNER in a meeting held on 13.1. 2010 and 19.5.2010 in the Ministry of Civil 
Aviation. The Ministry of Civil Aviation has inst ructed the Airports Authority of India to do 
the needful. Regarding the upgradation of ex isting airports, NEC ha s already funded the 
upgradation of 10 Airports in the region. Due to  the problem of land acquisition, two airports 
viz;  Dibrugarh (Assam) and Umroi (Meghalaya) are yet to be completed by the AAI. In 
order to make the non-functional airport at Tezu, operational, the NEC has accorded 100% 
financial support.  
4.2.4 Keeping in view the importa nce of the Sector, the Hon’ ble Minister himself took a 
meeting on 4.10.10 to discuss issues related with the development of Airports in the North 
Eastern Region which was attende d by senior officers from Air ports Authority of India and 
Ministry of Civil Aviation. 
 
Further Recommendation 
4.2.5 The Committee has found the action take n reply of the Ministry to be too 
general to be commented upon.  The Committe e has not been apprised of the current 
scenario with respect to the development of airports and air connectivity.  The 
Committee calls upon the Ministry to send a comprehensive status report to it 
immediately. 
 
 
 
 
 30

Recommendation: 
4.2.6 The Committee understands that improving connectivity is the only way to develop 
North Eastern Region and the Government should accord top priority to it. The Committee 
recommends that the Government should expedite  all the projects on hand for linking the 
States of the region through rail  network.   The target now fixed for the co mpletion of the 
projects is 2016. Though the target year is fa r away, yet the Committee desires that the 
Government should stick to this targeted period.  
(Para 3.3.18) 
Action Taken: 
4.2.7 The para has been referred to the Minist ry of Railways for s eeking their comments 
and the same are awaited. 
4.2.8 However, Ministry of DoNER has been pur suing the projects to facilitate the States’ 
efforts. The works on all the railway lines to co nnect the State capitals are at different stages 
of progress. The NEF Railways face problems of land acquisition and finalization of the rail 
alignment and for this, regular review meetings are being held with the state representatives.  
Further Recommendation 
4.2.9 The Committee reiterates its recommendation  that the Government should stick 
to the target for linking the States of th e region through rail network. The Committee 
expresses its displeasure over the fact that Ministry of Railways has not furnished its 
comments even after such a long time. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of 
DoNER should pursue the matter with the Ministry of Railways.  
 
4.3 MONITORING MECHANISM 
Recommendation: 
4.3.1 The Committee further recommends that there should be a separate wing of the 
Central Vigilance Commission ex clusively for North Eastern Region to oversee proper 
utilization of public funds for NER projects, from the vigilance angle.  
(Para 3.4.6)  
4.3.2 The Committee is also of the view that since huge amount of money is being spent on 
various projects in NE region and there is  a general feeling of misappropriation and 
siphoning of funds and that so me underground groups are also  illegally receiving some 
portion of funds, a post of Joint Director, CBI is required to be created for NE Region, to 
look into such cases. 
(Para 3.4.7) 
Action Taken: 
4.3.3 Since the recommendations concern DOP&T, these have been referred to them for 
taking further necessary appropriate action.  
 
Further Recommendation: 
4.3.4 The Committee desires to be apprised immediately of the response of the 
Government. 
 
 
 31

4.4 KEY AREAS AND PROJECTS UNDER LOOK EAST POLICY  
Recommendation: 
4.4.1 The Committee is of the considered view t hat various road projects linking the region 
with neighbouring landlocked countries could be of great help in increasing border trade 
with neighbouring countries and tackling insurgency in the region. The Committee also feels 
that the initiatives viz. Ka ladan multi-modal project, constr uction of Rih-Tidim and Rih-
Falam Road, Ashuganj (Bangladesh) as port of call , direct bus service from Kolkata to 
Agartala, project on Tri-latera l highway connecting Moreh to Maesot (Thailand) via Bagan 
(Myanmar) and improvement of Tamu Kalemyo Kalewa (TKK) Road in Myanmar, etc would 
greatly help opening commercial trade with the neighbouring countries of Bangladesh and 
Myanmar. The Committee, therefore, recommends  that under the ‘Look East Policy’, the 
Government may undertake steps towards completion of these projects at the earliest. 
(Para 3.6.10) 
Action Taken: 
4.4.2 The para has been referred to Ministry of  External Affairs for their comments which 
are awaited. 
 
Further Recommendation 
4.4.3 The Committee reiterates its recommenda tion that the Government should 
complete all the projects at the earliest . The Committee calls upon the Ministry of 
DoNER should pursue the matter with the Mini stry of External Affairs and apprise it 
immediately of their response in the matter.  
 
 
4.5 GENERAL RECOMMENDATIONS 
 
4.5.1 The Committee has been given to understand that there is huge potential of 
agriculture and allied sectors in the Nort h East and there is also a huge gap between 
potential and actual realization. In the agriculture and allied sect or, investment is low.  The 
Ministry should, therefore, unde rtake steps for ensuring special attention to th e agriculture 
sector.  
(Para 3.9) 
Action Taken: 
4.5.2 The matter  has  been  taken  up  with the Ministry of Agriculture.  In this regard, it is  
also pertinent to mention that recently the Department of Animal Husbandry, Dairying and 
Fisheries has organized a review meeting on 18 /5/2010 at Guwahati with the officials of NE 
States.  A number of issues have been iden tified and follow up actio n is being taken to 
improve the performance of this sector. 
 
4.5.3 A dedicated Small & Medium Enterprises (SME) Debt Fund is needed in the Region  
to help first time entrepreneurs, which may be considered for being set up by SIDBI in 
association with major Banks.  
 
4.5.4 Reduction  in  Guarantee  Fee (GF)  and Annual Service Fee (ASF) from 1.5% to 1%  
and from 0.75% to 0.5%, respectively, unde r the Credit Guarantee Scheme (CGS) of Credit 
Guarantee Fund Trust For Micro A nd Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)  is a welcome step. But, 
 32

for NER, CGTMSE may consider further reduc tion of 50% in GF and ASF to make it more 
effective in the NER. 
 
4.5.5 Interest Subvention provided in the agricultu re sector to commercial banks (lending 
at 7% with the shortfall being made up by Government of India) should be widened to 
include NBFC development finance institution (like NEDFi) not only for agricultural credit 
but also for promoting first generation entrepreneurs in the NER for projects upto Rs. 50 
lakh. The actual lending rate in such cases should be 7% with the deficit being made good by 
the Government of India. 
(Para 3.9) 
Action Taken: 
4.5.6 The matter has been taken up with the Depa rtment of Financial Services, Ministry 
of Finance.  Their response is awaited. 
 
Further Recommendation: 
4.5.7 The Committee feels that the government  should pay more attention to the 
agriculture and allied sectors in the region. The Committee takes serious note of the 
fact that the Department of Financial Serv ices, Ministry of Finance has not furnished 
its response even after a long gap. The Co mmittee feels that the Ministry of DoNER 
should have pursued the matter with the concerned Ministry and place the comments 
before the Committee.
